topics.titleTr: ChatGPT Eski Ses Modu Kapanıyor: GPT-Live'a Geç
topics.titleEn: ChatGPT Voice Retires Dec 11: Move to GPT-Live
topics.angle: how-to — migrate your voice workflow before Advanced/Standard Voice retire on Dec 11, 2026
topics.brief: OpenAI retires Advanced and Standard Voice on December 11, 2026, leaving GPT-Live. Sections: what changes and what carries over; re-recording custom instructions and voice choice; hands-free workflows (notes, commuting, brainstorming) rebuilt on GPT-Live; fallbacks when voice misbehaves. Verify: the exact retirement date and which tiers GPT-Live covers from the ChatGPT release notes. Primary sources: OpenAI's ChatGPT release notes and help center voice article. Keep it practical: a pre-Dec-11 checklist, then a tested daily voice routine so nobody loses their setup overnight.

topics.titleTr: Gemini Rambler: Dolgu Sözcüksüz Sesle Yazma
topics.titleEn: Gemini Rambler: Dictate Clean First Drafts
topics.angle: how-to — use Gemini's Rambler voice-typing to turn messy speech into clean drafts, hands-free
topics.brief: Google's November Pixel Drop added Rambler, a voice-typing mode that strips filler and structures speech into clean text. Sections: enabling Rambler and where it works; dictating an email, a doc outline, and meeting follow-ups; editing by voice; accuracy limits and privacy. Verify: device/rollout scope (which Pixels and regions) and whether it is on-device from the Pixel Drop coverage. Primary sources: Google's Pixel feature-drop post and Android Police's reporting. Include a short before/after of rambling speech becoming a tidy paragraph, and three tasks where dictation beats typing.

topics.titleEn: A Solo Weekly Review in 25 Minutes
topics.angle: checklist — a lightweight weekly planning ritual that clears the mind and sets next week, distinct from a performance self-review
topics.brief: Why do good intentions dissolve by Tuesday? Usually no weekly reset. Sections: the 25-minute timebox; clear the inboxes (email, notes, open loops); review calendar past and ahead; pick three outcomes; park everything else. Show a one-page template and how to keep it from ballooning. Verify: nothing contentious — frame GTD's weekly-review idea in plain terms and keep tool-agnostic. Primary sources: David Allen's weekly-review concept and one practitioner writeup. Contrast explicitly with a quarterly brag-doc review so readers don't conflate planning with self-evaluation.

topics.angle: deep-dive — the real cost of context-switching and a system to protect focused blocks
topics.brief: Context-switching quietly eats a developer's day. Sections: what research says about attention residue and recovery time; auditing your switches for a week; batching comms; designing two daily deep-work blocks; taming notifications and the AI-assistant tab-hopping trap. Verify: the attention-residue findings (Sophie Leroy) and any specific minutes-lost stats, flagged as estimates. Primary sources: Leroy's attention-residue paper and Cal Newport's deep-work framing. Avoid productivity-guru fluff; give a measurable one-week experiment with a simple log so readers can see their own switching cost.

topics.titleTr: Kitleni Sahiplen: Telegram ve WhatsApp Kanalları
topics.titleEn: Own Your Audience: Telegram & WhatsApp Channels
topics.angle: guide — build a direct, algorithm-proof audience with broadcast channels
topics.brief: Feeds throttle reach; broadcast channels deliver to everyone who opted in. Sections: WhatsApp Channels vs Telegram channels vs a newsletter; setting one up; what to post (and posting cadence); driving follows from your other platforms; measuring without vanity metrics. Verify: current WhatsApp Channels availability by region and any forwarding/discovery limits. Primary sources: Meta's WhatsApp Channels help docs and Telegram's channel documentation. Especially relevant for Turkish audiences where WhatsApp and Telegram dominate. Close with a 30-day plan to seed the first 500 followers.

topics.titleTr: İzlenme Süresi İçin Kurgu: Görüntülenme Değil
topics.titleEn: Edit for Watch Time, Not Just Views
topics.angle: deep-dive — editing techniques that lift average watch time and completion, the signals algorithms reward
topics.brief: Views are vanity; retention is the metric platforms actually rank on. Sections: reading the retention graph; the first-two-second hook; pattern interrupts, b-roll and captions; cutting dead air; loops and open loops that boost rewatches. Show a retention curve before and after edits. Verify: that TikTok, Reels and Shorts weight completion/average watch time, citing each platform's creator guidance. Primary sources: TikTok and YouTube creator documentation on watch time. End with an edit checklist you can apply to an existing clip to claw back the drop-off.

topics.titleTr: Tıklama Oranını Düşüren Kapak Görseli Hataları
topics.titleEn: Thumbnail Mistakes That Kill Your CTR
topics.angle: mistakes — the common thumbnail errors that tank click-through, and how to fix each
topics.brief: Great videos die behind weak thumbnails. Sections: too much text; low contrast at small sizes; faces with no emotion; clickbait that mismatches the title; ignoring mobile scale. For each mistake, a fix and a quick A/B idea. Verify: that CTR is title+thumbnail combined and how YouTube's thumbnail test tools report results. Primary sources: YouTube Help on thumbnails and its A/B thumbnail-test feature. Include a pre-publish thumbnail checklist and a note on keeping a consistent visual style so a channel is recognizable in a crowded feed.

topics.titleTr: Alıcılar AI'ya Sorunca Markan Anılıyor mu?
topics.titleEn: Is Your Brand Cited When Buyers Ask AI?
topics.angle: checklist — a repeatable monthly audit of whether ChatGPT, Gemini and Google AI Mode cite your brand
topics.brief: AEO theory is covered; this is the operational audit. Sections: building a prompt set of real buyer questions; running them across ChatGPT, Gemini and AI Mode; logging whether you're cited and how you're described; fixing naming inconsistency and thin third-party mentions; tracking month over month. Verify the Seer Interactive finding that cited brands earn ~35% more organic clicks, and query fan-out mechanics, flagged as correlational. Primary sources: Google Search Central on AI features and the Seer Interactive study. Provide a spreadsheet layout and a scoring rubric readers can reuse.

topics.titleTr: Dönüştüren Webinar: Yalın Bir Oyun Planı
topics.titleEn: Webinars That Convert: A Lean Playbook
topics.angle: guide — run a small-team webinar that actually drives pipeline, not just registrations
topics.brief: Registrations are easy; conversions are the point. Sections: picking a problem-first topic; a promo sequence that fills seats; a 40-minute structure with one clear CTA; live-to-replay follow-up emails; the three metrics that matter (show-up rate, engaged minutes, booked calls). Verify: realistic show-up-rate benchmarks and that replays outconvert live for many B2B funnels, flagged as varies-by-source. Primary sources: a reputable webinar benchmark report and your email tool's automation docs. Include a one-week run-of-show and a post-webinar follow-up template so a solo marketer can execute it.

topics.titleTr: Bir Öğleden Sonrada Dönüştüren Lead Magnet
topics.titleEn: Build a Lead Magnet in an Afternoon
topics.angle: how-to — design a high-converting, low-effort lead magnet and the opt-in around it
topics.brief: A lead magnet earns the email; most are too big to finish and too generic to want. Sections: picking a narrow, urgent problem; formats that convert (checklist, template, mini-audit) over a 40-page ebook; writing the opt-in copy; delivery and the first nurture email; avoiding GDPR/KVKK consent mistakes. Verify: that specific, outcome-named magnets beat broad ebooks, and consent-wording requirements. Primary sources: a conversion-benchmark source and official GDPR/KVKK consent guidance. Include three magnet templates and a one-afternoon build plan from idea to live opt-in.

topics.titleTr: Gemini Artık Senin Yerine Arıyor ve İş Yapıyor
topics.titleEn: Gemini Can Now Call and Do Tasks for You
topics.angle: deep-dive — what Gemini's agentic calling and in-app task actions actually do, with limits and privacy trade-offs
topics.brief: The November Pixel Drop lets Gemini place calls from your number to check stock or book reservations, and handle tasks in supported apps like grocery and rideshare. Sections: what it can and can't do; how it asks before acting; where tasks still fail; the privacy and consent questions of an AI calling on your behalf. Verify: device and region scope, and which apps are supported, from the Pixel Drop coverage. Primary sources: Google's Pixel feature-drop post and Android Police/Android Guys reporting. Keep it grounded and skeptical about reliability, not breathless.

topics.titleTr: 2026'da Onarım Hakkı: Neleri Kendin Tamir Edebilirsin?
topics.titleEn: Right to Repair in 2026: What You Can Fix
topics.angle: guide — where right-to-repair laws now stand and how to actually repair your own devices
topics.brief: Repair is finally getting easier, but the picture is uneven. Sections: what recent EU and US state right-to-repair rules require (parts, manuals, pairing); phones and laptops you can realistically fix; parts-pairing traps that still block DIY; tools and first repairs worth trying. Verify: the EU repairability/ecodesign rules and which US states' laws are in force, flagged with dates. Primary sources: the EU's right-to-repair directive pages and iFixit's repairability reporting. Make the counterpoint that 'repairable on paper' isn't always repairable in practice, with concrete examples.

topics.titleTr: C2PA: Bir Fotoğrafın Gerçek Olduğunu Kanıtlamak
topics.titleEn: C2PA: Proving a Photo Is Real
topics.angle: deep-dive — how Content Credentials (C2PA) attach provenance to media and where they break down
topics.brief: As deepfakes spread, provenance beats detection. Sections: what C2PA/Content Credentials record; how a camera or AI tool signs an image and how edits update the manifest; checking credentials in a viewer; the weak points (stripped metadata, screenshots, unsigned sources). Verify: which cameras, platforms and AI tools now support C2PA, and that metadata can be removed, breaking the chain. Primary sources: the C2PA specification site and the Content Authenticity Initiative. Contrast with watermarking approaches and explain why neither alone solves trust, closing with what a cautious reader should check.

topics.titleEn: Get Your Store Ready for AI Shopping Agents
topics.angle: guide — what merchants must do so an AI agent (ChatGPT Wallet / agentic checkout) can buy from them
topics.brief: ChatGPT Wallet (Nov 13) lets agents buy on a user's behalf after approval; stores that aren't agent-readable get skipped. Sections: structured product data and feeds; a checkout an agent can complete; the Agentic Commerce Protocol basics; trust signals (returns, reviews) agents weigh; measuring agent-driven orders. Verify: Wallet rollout scope and how agentic checkout authenticates from the launch coverage. Primary sources: OpenAI's agentic commerce documentation and reporting on ChatGPT Wallet. Frame it as early but strategic, and separate confirmed capabilities from speculation so founders don't overbuild.

topics.titleTr: Tek Kişilik Micro-SaaS Fikrini Nasıl Doğrularsın?
topics.angle: how-to — validate a niche micro-SaaS before writing code, as a solo founder
topics.brief: Most micro-SaaS fail from building before validating. Sections: finding a painful niche problem; talking to ten potential users without leading them; a landing-page smoke test with a waitlist; a concierge/manual MVP before automation; the signal threshold to greenlight building. Verify: the Mom Test interview principles and realistic smoke-test conversion ranges, flagged as rough. Primary sources: Rob Fitzpatrick's The Mom Test and a credible indie-hacker validation writeup. Keep it concrete with a two-week validation sprint and the kill criteria that tell a founder to walk away early.

topics.titleTr: Yeni SaaS İçin KVKK ve GDPR Uyum Listesi
topics.titleEn: KVKK & GDPR: A New SaaS Compliance Checklist
topics.angle: checklist — the privacy basics a new SaaS must cover under Turkey's KVKK and the EU GDPR
topics.brief: A startup can ship fast and still avoid privacy landmines. Sections: lawful basis and consent; privacy policy and data-processing records; data subject rights (access, deletion); processor agreements with your vendors; KVKK's VERBIS registration and data-localization nuances versus GDPR. Verify: whether VERBIS registration applies to your size, and cross-border transfer rules, flagged as not legal advice. Primary sources: Turkey's KVKK authority (kvkk.gov.tr) and the official GDPR text/EU guidance. Deliver a prioritized checklist for a pre-revenue SaaS, separating must-do-now from can-wait items.

topics.titleEn: Cheaper AI, Thinner Margins? Price Your App
topics.angle: comparison — how falling model prices (Fable 5.2, Gemini Flash) reshape the unit economics of an AI product
topics.brief: Fable 5.2 shipped ~20% cheaper and Flash-class models keep falling, yet many AI products still lose money per user. Sections: mapping cost per request to your pricing; why cheaper tokens don't guarantee margin (retries, context, tool calls); choosing a model tier per task; caching and routing to protect gross margin; pricing models that survive price swings. Verify: the Fable 5.2 price-cut figure and current Flash-class pricing, dated. Primary sources: Anthropic and Google pricing pages. Close with a simple unit-economics worksheet a founder can fill in for their own app.
